regional.headline: MERS-CoV. Severe respiratory disease acquired from dromedary camels.
regional.geography: MERS-CoV. Severe respiratory disease acquired from dromedary camels.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.incubation: 1–9 days after tick bite; 5–13 days after blood contact.
regional.syndrome: Abrupt fever, myalgia, severe headache, then haemorrhagic manifestations, hepatic dysfunction and DIC. Case fatality ranges from 5% to 40%. Nosocomial outbreaks among healthcare workers are a defining feature.
regional.headline: The most geographically widespread tick-borne virus causing human haemorrhagic fever; a WHO priority pathogen requiring high-level containment.
regional.prevention: Tick protection, safe slaughter practice, and strict barrier nursing with full PPE. No licensed vaccine (a Bulgarian inactivated vaccine has limited use).
regional.geography: Africa, the Balkans, Middle East, Central and South Asia, western China; expanding with Hyalomma range into Spain and southern Europe.
regional.evidence_note: Virus, viral RNA or specific antibody found in the reservoir host or in livestock, with no human case reported. The virus is present in the country; whether it has ever infected a person there is unknown.
